h1: The 6 Best UPS Battery Backups for NAS Devices, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best UPS Battery Backups for NAS: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 UPS battery backups for NAS drives, scored on waveform, capacity, USB shutdown signaling, AVR and battery replacement.
summary: The CyberPower CP850PFCLCD is the safest all-round UPS for a NAS, with a pure sine wave output, automatic voltage regulation and an LCD readout. The APC 850VA suits a multi-bay NAS that shares the UPS with a router, and the APC BE650G1 is the proven value pick. The Ubiquiti UniFi UPS Tower is for UniFi homes, and the WALLECUBE is a niche but purpose-built option for DC-powered NAS boxes.
intro: People shop for a NAS UPS by how many minutes of runtime it promises, and that is the wrong yardstick. A NAS does not need to stay on during an outage. It needs a clean, orderly shutdown before the battery runs out, so the file system closes properly and no RAID array is left rebuilding. That means the feature to hunt for is USB signaling that tells the NAS to shut itself down, not a bigger battery.

This ranking sorts six UPS units around that idea. We reviewed spec sheets and listings for capacity in VA and watts, output waveform, voltage regulation, USB connectivity, battery replaceability and ecosystem fit. Runtime figures are missing from most listings, and they depend on your drives and load, so we do not quote any. Check your NAS manual for its supported UPS list before buying.

products.name: CyberPower CP850PFCLCD PFC Sinewave UPS Battery Backup and Surge Protector
products.verdict: A pure sine wave UPS with AVR, an LCD and USB signaling, which is what modern NAS power supplies want.
products.description:
The CP850PFCLCD is an 850VA unit with PFC sine wave output, automatic voltage regulation, an LCD display and USB connectivity. It is built for computers and network gear with active power factor correction supplies.

It ranks first because the output waveform matters more for a NAS than for most devices. Many modern NAS and mini PC power supplies use active PFC, and some of them misbehave or switch off on the stepped, approximated waveform that cheaper battery backups produce during an outage. A pure sine wave removes that risk. AVR corrects low or high mains voltage without draining the battery, which extends battery life in areas with unstable power, and the LCD shows load and runtime in real time.

Buy it for a two- to four-bay NAS, especially one with an APFC power supply. The caveat is that CyberPower is a general-purpose brand, so check your NAS vendor's compatibility list before assuming the USB signal will be accepted.
pros: Pure sine wave suits APFC supplies
LCD shows load at a glance
USB lets the NAS shut down safely
cons: Costs more than basic Back-UPS units
products.idealFor: Buyers whose NAS or mini PC uses an APFC-equipped power supply.
products.skipIf: You only need basic surge protection on a tight budget.

products.name: APC UPS 850VA/450W UPS Battery Backup & Surge Protector for PC, Router, NAS
products.verdict: APC's 850VA unit, rated for NAS, router and PC loads with USB shutdown signaling.
products.description:
This APC Back-UPS offers 850VA and 450W, is listed for PC, router and NAS use, and includes USB shutdown signaling and surge protection.

It takes second place because it has the headroom for a multi-bay NAS plus a router or modem on the same unit. APC's USB signaling is recognized by almost every NAS operating system through a standard UPS protocol, which is why this brand is the one most guides default to. It loses to the CyberPower because Back-UPS class units usually output a stepped approximation of a sine wave on battery rather than a true one, so a few APFC supplies can trip. In practice, most NAS power supplies cope.

Choose it for a four- or six-bay NAS at home or a small office where the router also needs to stay alive through a short outage. Verify your NAS model's UPS list.
pros: Router can share the same UPS
cons: Battery output is not pure sine
products.idealFor: Buyers with a multi-bay NAS or who also need to protect a router on the same UPS.
products.skipIf: Your NAS has a sensitive APFC power supply.

products.name: APC UPS 650VA/390W Battery Backup & Surge Protector for PC, NAS | BE650G1
products.verdict: A widely used 650VA APC with USB signaling and a standard, replaceable battery.
products.description:
The BE650G1 provides 650VA and 390W, is rated for PC and NAS, has USB connectivity for shutdown signaling and uses a standard replaceable battery.

It is third because it covers a typical two-bay NAS with room to spare, and it has a long track record. The replaceable battery is the detail that counts. A UPS battery typically lasts three to five years, and a model that lets you swap in a new one at low cost outlasts the units that get thrown away. It ranks below the 850VA model because the 390W ceiling leaves less margin for a bigger NAS, a router and a switch together.

Buy it for a one- or two-bay NAS plus a modem. Skip it if you plan to add a drive enclosure or a mini PC to the same outlet.
pros: Right size for a two-bay NAS
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a proven, widely compatible general-purpose NAS UPS.
products.skipIf: You will add several devices to the same unit.

products.name: Ubiquiti UniFi UPS Tower 1000VA/600W Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS-Tower)
products.verdict: A 1000VA/600W tower with UniFi monitoring, sized for a NAS plus the network gear.
products.description:
The UniFi UPS Tower provides 1000VA and 600W, integrates with the UniFi ecosystem and uses a tower form factor suited to a shelf or rack setup. The listing highlights higher capacity for combined NAS and networking loads.

It ranks fourth because its main advantage is relevant only to a particular owner. If your router, switches and access points are UniFi, the UPS reports into the same console, so you see battery state and outage alerts alongside the rest of the network. At 600W it has the most capacity here, which fits a larger NAS plus a switch and a gateway. At $200 to $500, it costs the most, and its NAS signaling depends on how the UniFi integration handles shutdown commands.

Choose it if you run UniFi and want one console for everything. Otherwise an APC or CyberPower gives the same protection for less.
pros: Tower form fits shelf or rack
products.idealFor: Buyers already using UniFi networking gear who want integrated monitoring.
products.skipIf: You do not use UniFi and want the best price.

products.name: APC UPS 600VA/330W UPS Battery Backup for Computer, Router, NAS, BE600M1
products.verdict: The smallest APC here, enough for a single-bay NAS and a router.
products.description:
The BE600M1 gives 600VA and 330W, is listed for computer, router and NAS use, includes USB shutdown signaling, and uses a standard replaceable battery.

It ranks fifth because it is the minimum viable option. A single-bay NAS and a modem sit comfortably inside 330W, and you still get USB signaling and a battery you can replace. It falls behind the BE650G1 only by a small margin of capacity, and is a similar product in practice.

Buy it if your NAS is a single-bay or two-bay unit with light drives and your router is low-power. Do not use it for larger arrays, because the load will leave very little runtime, and pushing a UPS near its limit shortens battery life.
pros: Compact for a desk or shelf
products.idealFor: Budget-conscious buyers with a single-bay NAS or basic home server.
products.skipIf: Your NAS has more than two bays.

products.name: WALLECUBE NAS UPS Compatible for: Synology, Ugreen, TerraMaster, QNAP. 150W DC Uninterruptible Power Supply with Remote APP Control
products.verdict: A compact 150W DC UPS built for DC-powered NAS and mini PCs, with app control.
products.description:
The WALLECUBE is a 150W DC UPS that lists compatibility with Synology, Ugreen, TerraMaster and QNAP. It offers remote app control and a compact home-server form factor, and it supplies DC output rather than a mains outlet.

It finishes sixth because it only suits NAS units that run on an external DC adapter, which is typical of small 2- and 4-bay home models and mini PCs. Those owners can skip the double conversion of a mains UPS, which wastes some power as heat. It does not replace a conventional UPS for a NAS with an internal AC supply, and the listing does not describe a shutdown signaling method, so check how it tells the NAS to power down.

Pick it if your NAS uses a barrel-plug DC adapter that matches the unit's voltage. Check connector and voltage compatibility carefully before ordering.
products.idealFor: Buyers with a DC-powered NAS from a supported vendor who want purpose-built compatibility.
products.skipIf: Your NAS plugs into the wall with a standard AC cord.

methodology.title: Output waveform
methodology.description: We looked for pure sine wave output, since APFC power supplies in newer NAS and mini PC hardware prefer it over stepped waveforms.

methodology.title: Shutdown signaling
methodology.description: We checked for USB connectivity, as the NAS needs a signal to shut down cleanly before the battery runs out.

methodology.title: Capacity headroom
methodology.description: We compared VA and watt ratings against typical NAS, router and switch loads, with attention to leaving margin.

methodology.title: Battery serviceability
methodology.description: We favored units with replaceable batteries, because a UPS battery is a consumable and replacement is cheaper than a new unit.

methodology.title: Ecosystem and value
methodology.description: We considered integration such as UniFi monitoring or app control, and weighed each unit's price bracket against what it adds.

whatMatters.detail: A pure sine wave UPS produces a smooth AC waveform on battery, while a simulated one uses steps that approximate it. Active PFC power supplies in some NAS and mini PCs can reject the stepped version and shut off. Look for the words pure sine wave or PFC sinewave in the listing.

VA is the apparent power and watts the real power the UPS can deliver, and the watt rating is the limit that counts. Add up the NAS, router and any switch loads in watts and stay at or below about 60 to 70 percent of the UPS rating. Check the watt figure on the listing, not just the VA.

A USB cable lets the UPS tell the NAS that mains has failed and the battery is draining. The NAS then shuts down cleanly on a timer or at a set battery level. Most NAS operating systems support APC and CyberPower units, so check your vendor's UPS compatibility page.

AVR boosts or trims the incoming voltage during a brownout or surge without switching to battery. It saves battery wear in areas with unstable power and keeps the NAS running through small dips. Look for AVR on the spec list, since many cheaper units omit it.

UPS batteries are sealed lead-acid cells that wear out in about three to five years. A unit with a standard replaceable battery costs far less to keep going than one you have to discard. Check for user replaceable or standard battery wording, and note the replacement cartridge model.

howToChoose.subheading: Pure Sine Wave vs Simulated Sine Wave

cards.label: Pure sine wave
cards.text: A smooth waveform that every power supply handles, including active PFC types. It costs a little more. Picks: CyberPower CP850PFCLCD.

cards.label: Simulated sine wave
cards.text: A stepped output that works with most NAS power supplies and costs less. A few APFC supplies can trip. Picks: the three APC Back-UPS models.

howToChoose.note: Default to pure sine wave if your NAS or mini PC manual mentions active PFC.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: USB shutdown signaling, enough watts for the drives plus the router, and a replaceable battery. Runtime matters less than a clean shutdown.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The APC UPS 650VA/390W BE650G1 is the sensible pick for a two-bay media server, and the APC 850VA unit suits a larger array.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Your NAS holds irreplaceable data, has an APFC supply, or sits in a place with unstable power. The CyberPower CP850PFCLCD adds sine wave output and AVR.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have a small NAS and rare outages. The APC BE600M1 gives you signaling and a replaceable battery for less.

faq.q: Will my NAS shut down automatically on a power cut?
faq.a: Yes, if the UPS is connected to the NAS by USB and the NAS supports UPS monitoring. You set a delay or battery threshold in the NAS settings. Check your vendor's compatibility list before buying.

faq.q: What mistake do people make when sizing a UPS for a NAS?
faq.a: They pick a unit by VA instead of watts and run it near its limit. A heavily loaded UPS has less runtime and wears out faster. Aim for a total load below about two thirds of the watt rating.

faq.q: Is a pure sine wave UPS worth it over a cheaper one?
faq.a: It is if your NAS or mini PC has an active PFC power supply, since some of those misbehave on a stepped waveform. For many older or simpler supplies a standard Back-UPS is fine. The NAS manual or vendor forum usually says which.

faq.q: How do I set up the USB connection?
faq.a: Plug the NAS into the battery-backed outlets, connect the UPS USB port to the NAS, and enable UPS support in the NAS software. Then set the shutdown trigger. Run a test pull of the mains plug once to confirm the NAS shuts down.

faq.q: Can I plug a laser printer into the UPS?
faq.a: It is better not to, because laser printers draw a large surge when they warm up. Put them on a surge-only outlet if there is one. Keep the battery outlets for the NAS, router and switch.

faq.q: When should I replace the battery?
faq.a: Most UPS batteries last three to five years in normal conditions. Replace it when the unit reports a battery fault or the runtime falls sharply. Standard replaceable batteries make the job a quick swap.

finalTake: The CyberPower CP850PFCLCD is the best UPS for a NAS, because its pure sine wave output, AVR and USB signaling cover the failures that matter. The APC 850VA is the sensible choice for a bigger array that shares the unit with a router. The APC BE650G1 is the value pick, the Ubiquiti suits UniFi homes, and the WALLECUBE is only for DC-powered NAS boxes.
